subject.title: [Bug]: Memory detection skips macOS (darwin) — os.freemem() / os.totalmem() never reported to agent on non-Linux platforms

question: Should macOS startup optimization hints target all Apple Silicon Macs like Linux ARM, or only low-memory Darwin hosts?
rationale: The code change is small, but applying the current Linux ARM rule to Darwin would show low-power/Pi-style guidance on high-memory Apple Silicon machines unless maintainers choose a narrower macOS policy and update the copy.

options.title: Low-memory Darwin only
options.body: Add Darwin support only for genuinely constrained Macs, keep Linux ARM behavior unchanged, update the note wording, and cover Darwin low/high-memory tests.

options.title: Match Linux ARM behavior
options.body: Treat all Darwin ARM hosts as startup-tuning targets and make the broader Apple Silicon guidance explicit in copy and tests.

options.title: Keep Linux-only hints
options.body: Reject or defer macOS startup hints if maintainers want this low-power doctor guidance to stay Linux-only for now.

recommendation.title: Low-memory Darwin only
recommendation.body: Add Darwin support only for genuinely constrained Macs, keep Linux ARM behavior unchanged, update the note wording, and cover Darwin low/high-memory tests.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored and merged the PR that introduced the startup optimization helper and Linux-only target policy.
